lede: Trump rules out Iran strikes before the midterms; oil eases; Nasdaq futures rebound on OpenAI revenue report.

single_name_moves.venue: Thu close, more than -7% on OpenAI revenue report (CNBC)

geo_headlines: NO IRAN STRIKES BEFORE THE MIDTERMS, TRUMP SAYS. President Trump said Thursday the US will not attack Iran before the November 3 midterms and cited "productive discussions" with Tehran (CNN, Al Jazeera), even as the Pentagon prepares options (New York Times). **Oil eased overnight: Brent December is $102.84 (-1.4%) and WTI November $90.61 (-1.0%), after Brent settled at $104.28 Thursday.** Iranian media reported explosions in the southern Strait of Hormuz (Al Jazeera).

AI JITTERS HIT CHIPS; FUTURES REBOUND. Thursday the Nasdaq 100 fell 1.39%, its steepest drop in seven weeks, and chip stocks 3.4%, after reports that OpenAI's annualized revenue was about $50 billion, roughly $20 billion below figures previously circulated (CNBC, FT). Overnight, Bloomberg reported OpenAI expects at least $70 billion by year end (Yahoo Finance). Nasdaq 100 futures 31,198.50 (+0.74%), S&P 500 futures 7,842.25 (+0.33%) as of 6:51 AM ET.

STOCKS: S&P 500 -0.47%; DOW UP. The S&P 500 fell to 7,765.36, 0.69% below Tuesday's record; the Nasdaq Composite fell 1.25% and the Dow rose 0.10%. More than two-thirds of S&P 500 members rose as money rotated to defensives (CNBC-TV18).

BONDS PASSED THE TEST. The $22 billion 30-year sold at 5.618% with indirect bidders taking 72.3%, above the 68% average (CNBC). The 10-year closed at 5.22% (-6bp) and the 30-year at 5.60% (-7bp) on Treasury's curve. Jobless claims were 197,000, near 57-year lows (Reuters). FedWatch: October hike 18.8%, from 17.7%; December 84.8%.

HURRICANE ISAIAS NEARS THE GULF COAST. At 4 AM CDT the storm had 110 mph winds and was likely to become a major hurricane this morning, with landfall tonight or early Saturday; warnings run from Ocean Springs, Mississippi, to the Florida Panhandle (National Hurricane Center). Chevron and Shell shut in output at nine Gulf facilities (investingLive). Gold $4,205.20 (+1.2%); bitcoin $82,516 (+1.0%).

TODAY: MICHIGAN SENTIMENT, DELTA. Delta reports before the open (webcast 10:00 AM). University of Michigan sentiment, preliminary October, at 10:00 AM; consensus 47.6-48.0 vs 48.1 in September. Bank earnings start Tuesday.
client_frame_short: Two things changed overnight. President Trump said the US will not strike Iran before the November midterms, and oil eased back to about $103. And after Thursday's AI scare, when a report on OpenAI's revenue knocked chip stocks down 3.4%, a second report said OpenAI expects $70 billion by year end, and Nasdaq futures are up. **Bonds also passed a big test: strong demand at the 30-year auction pulled long yields down from their 24-year highs.** For clients, nothing here calls for changes; earnings season starts Tuesday with the banks.
client_frame:
If a client calls this morning, the story is a calmer Friday after a jumpy Thursday.

Iran: President Trump said the US will not attack Iran before the November 3 midterms and called talks with Tehran productive. The Pentagon is still drawing up options, and Iran is still harassing tankers in Hormuz, so the risk has been pushed back rather than removed. Oil reacted: Brent is about $103, down from $104.28 at Thursday's settle.

AI stocks: Thursday's selloff came from a report that OpenAI's annualized revenue was about $50 billion, roughly $20 billion below what had been circulating. Chip stocks fell 3.4% and the Nasdaq 100 1.4%. Overnight, a second report said OpenAI expects at least $70 billion by year end, and Nasdaq futures are up about 0.7%. The lesson is how sensitive these stocks are to a single data point after a big run. Two-thirds of the S&P 500 still rose Thursday.

Bonds: this week's 10-year and 30-year auctions both drew strong demand. The 10-year yield closed at 5.22%, down from 5.31% on Monday, and the 30-year at 5.60%. Buyers are showing up at these levels, which takes some pressure off stocks.

The Fed: markets put October hike odds near one in five and December near 85%. Jobless claims came in at 197,000, near 57-year lows, so the job market is not giving the Fed a reason to wait.

Why it matters: concentration risk in AI-linked stocks is real, and Thursday showed it. That is a reason for rebalancing discipline, not for selling.

For clients, the message holds: high-quality bonds pay more than 5% for a decade, and long-term equity plans do not need changing. What would change the view: a 10-year close above 5.40% (now 5.22%), a 30-year above 5.75% (now 5.60%), or actual US strikes on Iran that keep Brent well above $105 (now about $103, and strikes are on hold until after the midterms).
